planner: hand-written demo plan (muse-2bit-ttft, preliminary node contracts)

nodes.title: Pin the stock llama.cpp tree, the official Muse NVFP4 checkpoint, the imatrix and the prompts by digest, and record the disk grant and memory cap.
Extend the stock converter so it reads the stacked Muse NVFP4 experts and their scale planes, then write the NVFP4 GGUF pack.
Apply the per-expert NVFP4 scale tensors in the Muse graph so the NVFP4 pack computes the same values as the checkpoint.
Build the base engine E0 (stock plus scale wiring) and run one cold, capped NVFP4 inference.

Write a precision recipe and requantize the NVFP4 pack to a 2-bit pack: routed gate and up experts to IQ2_XXS and down experts to Q2_K (the down projection is the most sensitive to low bits), everything else kept at its source type.
Record which experts the 2-bit pack routes to on calibration prompts that do not overlap the lab prompts.
Port the profile-seeded expert weight cache (the earlier time-to-first-token change) onto E0 for the Muse layer and expert shapes, off by default.
Build candidate engine E1 (E0 plus the seeded cache) and package it for the lab arms.

Size the server prefill batch so each lab prompt is prefilled in as few micro-batches as the device budget allows, give the rest of the budget to the MoE expert cache, and check both on capped loads of E1 with the 2-bit pack.

Send E0, E1, both packs, the profile, the prefill batch plan and the lab task for arms A, B, C and D, with the paired accuracy test (accuracy_2bit, A against B), to the lab manager. Arm A keeps --moe-cache-mib 61440; arms B, C and D take the plan's --moe-cache-mib, and only arm D its -b and -ub.
